ops-announce-bot: Heads-up — we are reshuffling dedicated L10e micro-pool burst windows and introducing a new two-tier burst policy for EU-North and AMS zones. Details below. :loudspeaker:

maya: TL;DR: L10e micro-pools go live in eu-north-1 and ams-1 next Tue (2026-04-07). New burst policy limits spot/rotational bursts to 4h contiguous windows and adds reserved burst priority for committed customers.

ryan: What does this mean for existing reserved customers? Will latency SLAs change?

maya: Reserved capacity unaffected. SLA for reserved unchanged. Rotational/spot users will see capped continuous burst length; we'll still allow queued short bursts. Expect p99 token latency unchanged for reserved.

leo: Ops: will this require any config changes for customers using auto-reserve via CLI?

maya: No change required for reserved stacks. For auto-reserve scripts that rely on unlimited burst, switch to new flag `--burst-window 4h` or we'll auto-enforce.

sophia: Cost note: projected unit cost for rotational bursts up ~8% when burst windows overlap peak hours — we recommend scheduling non-critical batch runs to off-peak.

ryan: Can we add a migration script or policy for customers hitting failures now?

maya: We're shipping a helper script: 
```
redwood reserve modify --pool l10e-eu-north --burst-window 4h --notify-team
```
We'll also auto-notify customers with active >8h bursts in the past 7 days.

oncall-bot: Allocation snapshot: l10e-eu-north micro-pools: Reserved: 62%, Rotational: 28%, Free: 10% (as of 2432100120)

leo: Ops action: SRE, please watch the first 48h after rollout for spillover to older GPU classes.

sophia: I'll update the cost docs and notify Partnerships + Sales package.

maya: Rollout schedule: canary 2026-04-05 08:00 UTC (10% traffic), wide 2026-04-07 02:00 UTC. Support playbook in #support pinned.

ryan: thanks — ping me when canary metrics are up.

maya: Will do. :rocket:
